articles.title: CJP assault case: Swatantra Bhardwaj gets regular bail after 3-week interim relief
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Tuesday granted regular bail to social media influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj in connection with the alleged assault on the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Tuesday granted regular bail to social media influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj in connection with the alleged assault on the father of a student activist during a protest at Jantar Mantar.Bhardwaj had earlier been granted three weeks' interim bail with strict conditions. The court has now granted him regular bail after considering his conduct during the interim bail period.A detailed order, including the bail conditions, is expected to be passed later in the day, according to news agency ANI.On September 15, the court had granted Bhardwaj three weeks' interim bail and said his conduct during the period would be considered before deciding his regular bail plea.It had barred him from posting, publishing or discussing the case, his defence or the complainant's family on social media or any media platform.He was also restrained from contacting the complainant, his daughter or any witness and from tampering with evidence.The court had observed that “bail is an expression of the court’s trust, and it is not a trophy to be displayed”, while cautioning against public celebrations following release on bail.Why was Bhardwaj arrested?Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr on September 4, hours after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protested outside the Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest over the alleged assault.The action followed outrage over an interview in which Bhardwaj claimed that he had “cracked the skull” of the student activist's father during the June 23 protest and that he escaped arrest because of his 'political connections'.Police, however, had disputed the severity of the injuries claimed by Bhardwaj, saying the man suffered a simple head injury during a scuffle.Bhardwaj was subsequently remanded to judicial custody on September 7 and lodged in Tihar Jail. He was released from the prison on September 18 after being granted interim bail.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Southern California once had so many of these mountain frogs that people could barely avoid stepping on them; now about 650 were released back into the wild
articles.summary: In the streams of Southern California’s mountains, the southern mountain yellow-legged frog has had a difficult few decades.
articles.body: In the streams of Southern California’s mountains, the southern mountain yellow-legged frog has had a difficult few decades. The species was once far more widespread, with historic accounts describing streams where frogs were so numerous that people could scarcely move without stepping around them. Finding them in the wild is a very different proposition; their remaining populations are scattered across parts of the San Gabriel, San Bernardino and San Jacinto mountains.Conservation teams released 653 captive-bred frogs into streams in the San Gabriel Mountains. The release is part of a longer recovery effort that has already returned thousands of Los Angeles Zoo-bred frogs to native habitat.Southern mountain yellow-legged frogs make a return to mountain streamsAccording to the Association of Zoos & Aquarium (AZAs), the release happened in two stages. On 19 August, 338 southern mountain yellow-legged frogs were taken to streams in the San Gabriel Mountains and released into their native environment. A further 315 followed on 27 August, bringing the total to 653. Every frog in this release was bred at the Los Angeles Zoo. Of those, 227 had been raised in a new bio-secure amphibian headstarting facility at the zoo, a development that has expanded the number of young frogs that can be raised under controlled conditions before being returned to the mountains.The release also takes the number of Los Angeles Zoo-bred frogs returned to the wild since the Southern Mountain Yellow-legged Frog Recovery Program began to nearly 7,000.Southern mountain yellow-legged frogs are raised under controlled conditionsThe new facility occupies a renovated section of the Los Angeles Zoo’s Children’s Discovery Center. It contains specialised tanks and life-support equipment designed to maintain suitable water conditions for the amphibians as they develop. Tadpoles can be vulnerable during their early development, so keeping them in a carefully controlled setting allows zoo staff to raise them until they are larger and more developed. They can then be released at a stage when they are better equipped to deal with predators and the other hazards found in natural streams.For the 227 frogs raised in the new facility, that process provided an expanded route from breeding and hatching to release. Byron Wusstig, curator of ectotherms at the Los Angeles Zoo said, “Seeing our new headstarting facility transition from a concept to a fully operational reality is a monumental milestone for the recovery of the southern mountain yellow-legged frog.”The work is not confined to Los Angeles. About 112 tadpoles bred at the zoo were also due to be transferred to the Santa Ana Zoo later in September for continued care.Why southern mountain yellow-legged frogs are now endangeredSouthern mountain yellow-legged frogs are adapted to perennial streams in parts of Southern California’s mountain ranges. They are relatively small, generally measuring between about 1.5 and 3.25 inches as adults.Brown and yellow are common colours, although individuals may also appear grey, reddish or greenish-brown. Dark spots and irregular markings help them blend into surfaces around their habitat, sometimes resembling moss or lichen. The yellow or pale orange colouring on the underside of the legs is the feature behind the species' common name.Their present distribution is a shadow of the species' former presence. Historical descriptions indicate that the frogs could once occur in large numbers along Southern California mountain streams, to the point where people moving through their habitat might have struggled to avoid stepping on them.The change has been severe enough for the International Union for Conservation of Nature to classify the southern mountain yellow-legged frog as Endangered.A recovery effort involving zoos and government agenciesThe releases are being carried out through a partnership led by the US Geological Survey. The programme brings together the Los Angeles Zoo, San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, Omaha’s Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium, the US Forest Service, the US Fish and Wildlife Service and the California Department of Fish and Wildlife.Other organisations have since joined the effort, including the Aquarium of the Pacific, Santa Ana Zoo, Big Bear Alpine Zoo and Birch Aquarium at Scripps. The network is expected to expand further.For the southern mountain yellow-legged frog, the San Gabriel Mountains are one of the places where that work is now taking place.Southern mountain yellow-legged frogs add another 653 to a long recovery effortThe 653 frogs released in August are not being treated as a standalone conservation event. They form part of an ongoing attempt to rebuild populations of a species that has become much less common across its former range.The Los Angeles Zoo has now contributed almost 7,000 captive-bred frogs to releases in the wild since the recovery programme began. The new headstarting facility gives the zoo another way to increase that contribution, particularly by allowing tadpoles to remain under controlled care until they reach a more suitable stage for release. The species can still be seen by visitors at the Los Angeles Zoo, where southern mountain yellow-legged frogs are displayed in the Living Amphibian, Invertebrate, and Reptile exhibit.You use AI every day. articles.title: US Immigration authority is making filing of forms online mandatory; says these are  two options
articles.summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced that it will soon mandate online filing for many immigration forms that have been available
articles.body: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced that it will soon mandate online filing for many immigration forms that have been available for e-filing for at least 180 days. The immigration authority shared a post on X (formerly Twitter), stating that “Digital submissions help us receive, store, and access information more efficiently, supporting stronger fraud detection, identity management, and national security screening.” The post also has a link to the ‘Online Filing Options’ website listing forms that are available for online filing, benefits of filing a form online, among others.There are two options for submitting forms from a USCIS online account, the webpage states. The first is filling out an online form electronically where you are guided step-by-step through the form to answer questions that are relevant to your form type and category. The second online filing option allows you to upload and submit a completed PDF file of your form and related evidence. Both filing options have similar features to manage your case in your online account.USCIS forms available to file onlineAlmost all USCIS forms can be filed online. Some of these are:AR-11 | Alien’s Change of Address CardEOIR-29 | Notice of Appeal to the Board of Immigration Appeals from a Decision of a DHS OfficerG-28I | Notice of Entry of Appearance as Attorney in Matters Outside the Geographical Confines of the United StatesG-325A | Biographic Information (for Deferred Action)G-325R | Biographic Information (Registration)G-845 | Verification RequestG-884 | Request for the Return of Original DocumentHow to fill out and file a USCIS form onlineStep 1: Sign in to your USCIS online account or create a USCIS online account, if you do not already have one. Go to our Sign Up page. If you need help creating a USCIS online account, please visit our How to Create a USCIS Online Account page.You must provide a valid email address and password to create a USCIS online account. The email address you provide will also be the username for your USCIS online account. The USCIS online account uses a two-factor authentication process. This means that in addition to entering your username and password, you must also enter a 1-time verification code that USCIS will send you by email, text message, or authentication app, each time you sign into your account. When you create your USCIS online account, you can select how you want to receive the 1-time verification code. If you select text message, enter your U.S. mobile phone number in the Mobile Number box (standard SMS/text messaging rates may apply). If you select the app option, the system will generate a code that you can scan or type into an authentication app that you have installed on your mobile device (such as Google Authenticator).To sign in to your USCIS online account using two-factor authentication:Every time you sign in to your USCIS online account, you must enter your email address and password and select “Sign In.”USCIS will then send you a 1-time verification code by email, text, or authentication app based on what you chose when you created your account. (You may change your delivery preference within your account.) Please allow a few minutes for delivery. If you selected the email option but you do not see a verification email in your inbox, make sure to check your junk mail or spam folder.Enter your 1-time verification code in the box and select “Submit.”If you have not received your verification code after 10 minutes, select “please request a new verification code.”Step 2: Select “File a Form Online.”Step 3: Select the form you want to file.Step 4: Select “Fill Out Form Fields Online.”Step 5: Complete all sections of your form.Fill out all sections of the form as completely as possible.Read the form instructions for information on completing fields when your answer is “zero” or “not applicable (N/A).”Step 6: Upload evidence.You may need to provide evidence when you file to support your application, petition, or request. These documents help us evaluate your form and verify information you have provided.Use these tips when uploading evidence:Use a scanner or photograph each document. Make sure each image you attach is clear and that all text is readable.Files must not be larger than 12MB.Files generally must be PDFs, JPGs, or JPEGs. For some forms, USCIS also accept files in TIF or TIFF format.Do not encrypt or password-protect your files.If your documents are in a foreign language, upload the original document, a certified English translation, and the translator’s certificate for each document.If USCIS require passport-style photos, you must either scan them or take a picture with your phone.Step 7: Review and digitally sign your form.Review the summary of the information you provided in your application, petition, or request. You may save and print a copy for your records.To digitally sign your application, petition, or request, enter your full legal name (first, middle, and last names) in the space provided. The system will affix your signature and the date to your online application. After you submit your application, petition, or request, you cannot make any changes.Step 8: Pay the filing fee, if applicable.You must pay with a valid credit or debit card or provide your bank routing and checking account numbers to have money taken directly from your U.S. bank account.After you make your payment, your form will be submitted. If there is no fee associated with your application, then the form will be submitted directly to USCIS.For most forms, you will immediately receive a receipt notice that contains your receipt number. For some forms, it may take up to 3 days to receive a receipt number. A receipt number is a unique number that applies to your specific case with USCIS. You can find your receipt number on your online account home page, and you can find a copy of your receipt notice under the Documents or Notices tab, as applicable.Step 9: View appointment notices.USCIS may schedule you for a biometric services appointment at an application support center. Log in to your USCIS online account for more information about your appointment.You must attend this appointment and provide biometric information, which may include your photograph, signature, and fingerprints.If you need to attend an interview, you will also receive an interview appointment notice in your account.Step 10: Respond to Requests for Evidence and upload unsolicited evidence.USCIS will notify you by text message or email (based on your preference) if you need to respond to a Request for Evidence (RFE).Log in to your USCIS online account and go to the “Documents or Notices” tab, as applicable, to view notices and respond to the RFE.While your case is pending, you may provide additional information, including evidence USCIS did not specifically request, about your case. If you do not have an open RFE, you can do this in the “Documents or Evidence” tab, as applicable. Look for the additional evidence uploader at the bottom of the tab.Step 11: Check the status of your case.Log in to your USCIS online account for details on the status of your case.Step 12: Send and receive secure messages.After you file a form, you will have access to a secure inbox to send messages to USCIS and receive responses to your questions.Step 13: Receive a decision.Log in to your USCIS online account to read details of the decision made on your case. For information on processing times for all forms, please visit our USCIS Processing Time Information page.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, time to resign': Rahul Gandhi as INDIA bloc march to EC stopped
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday called on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign as INDIA bloc MPs
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday called on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign as INDIA bloc MPs marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission of India headquarters over alleged discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, Time to resign,” Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X as he led the opposition MPs towards the ECI office.The march, which began from Parliament's Makar Dwar around 11 am, was stopped by security personnel near the Niti Aayog office. Several INDIA bloc MPs subsequently sat in protest, with opposition leaders later staging a dharna at Parliament Street.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule were among the opposition leaders participating in the march.INDIA bloc MPs stopped near Niti AayogVisuals showed Rahul Gandhi leading the march along with several INDIA bloc MPs, who were carrying placards and cutouts of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The opposition MPs were seeking Kumar's removal over alleged irregularities in the SIR process. The INDIA bloc had announced the march from Parliament to Nirvachan Sadan as part of its campaign against the Election Commission's handling of the electoral roll revision.The march was met with heavy security deployment in central Delhi. Barricades were placed along the route and Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed around Transport Bhawan ahead of the protest.After being prevented from proceeding towards the ECI headquarters, several opposition MPs sat in protest near Parliament Street.AAP said it would skip the march, with the party saying it would fight the issue through its own means.Opposition steps up attack over SIRThe protest comes amid an ongoing political confrontation between the opposition and the Election Commission over the SIR exercise and alleged discrepancies in voter rolls.The Supreme Court on Tuesday said it had not approved any modified version of Form 6 used for voter enrolment during the SIR process. CJI Surya Kant said, “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us.”The court issued notices to the Centre, ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and other officials while declining to pass an ex-parte interim order suspending Kumar.Ahead of the march, several opposition leaders criticised the Election Commission's handling of the SIR process. Congress and INDIA bloc leaders have demanded Kumar's removal, while the BJP has rejected the opposition's allegations.Mamata Banerjee has said the protests will continue until Kumar resigns and has also demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation.Congress MP Jairam Ramesh had said the march would be peaceful. The opposition has also announced district-level padyatras till October 8 and "Save votes, save the country" rallies from October 25 to November 25.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Four nations, four drills, one month: How the army is expanding its military partnerships
articles.summary: The army has held military exercises with four different counterparts from four different nations at virtually the same time.
articles.body: The army has held military exercises with four different counterparts from four different nations at virtually the same time. Exercise Yudh Abhyas, the 22nd edition of India's bilateral drill with the United States, was underway across Mahajan field firing range in Rajasthan and Auli in Uttarakhand, bringing in Arctic-trained American soldiers from Alaska's 11th Airborne Division for the high-altitude phase near the Line of Actual Control. Days apart, Exercise Mountain Guardian 2026 began with the UAE at Chaubatia in Uttarakhand, focused on mountain warfare and drone operations between a Bhairav Battalion contingent and UAE's Mountain Infantry Battalion. Further north, the ninth edition of KAZIND with Kazakhstan is being held at Oskemen, with a 60-member contingent drawn mainly from the Garhwal Rifles. And this week, the 18th edition of Exercise Nomadic Elephant with Mongolia concluded at Pithoragarh.Running several of these wargames almost simultaneously reflects how far Indian military diplomacy has evolved. For decades, India's defence partnerships were shaped by Cold War-era non-alignment, keeping formal engagement deliberately limited. That has changed substantially. Bilateral exercises now serve as working tools of foreign policy, letting India build interoperability across a wide range of militaries.Exercising with the US validates India's deepening defence-technology relationship, while the drills with the UAE reflect the growing defence relationship between the two strategic partners. KAZIND keeps India engaged with Central Asia, while Nomadic Elephant sustains cooperation with Mongolia, a country wedged between China and Russia that has consistently sought to diversify its partnerships.Hosting these exercises on Indian soil carries its own advantages. It lets a far larger number of Indian troops get exposed to tactics, techniques and procedures of these militaries as well as exposure to equipment. It allows India to control the terrain and objectives of the exercise, tailoring drills to test its own tactics. The drills also signal confidence and capability to visiting militaries, reinforcing India's position as a credible security partner rather than simply a participant.A source in the army has said Exercise Indra, India's biennial exercise with Russia, is to be held later this year, though an official date has not yet been announced. This isn't limited to these engagements either. The Army regularly exercises with other major militaries too, including France, the United Kingdom and Japan, while the Navy and Air Force run their own parallel exercises such as Malabar with the US, Japan and Australia.These exercises deliver direct military value. They expose Indian troops to different equipment, doctrines and combat environments, build interoperability at different levels and offers an opportunity to display indigenous systems to foreign militaries. For a country whose strategic autonomy is frequently tested by its neighbourhood, the ability to exercise simultaneously across such a varied set of partners demonstrates the room India has built for itself on the world stage.
